The '''2016–17 Ekstraklasa''' (also known as '''Lotto Ekstraklasa''' due to its [[Sponsor (commercial)|sponsorship]] by Totalizator Sportowy, Polish [[lottery]])<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.ekstraklasa.org/lotto-partnerem-tytularnym-ekstraklasy |title=LOTTO Partnerem Tytularnym Ekstraklasy |website=www.ekstraklasa.org |date=14 July 2016 |access-date=15 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160718034522/http://www.ekstraklasa.org/lotto-partnerem-tytularnym-ekstraklasy |archive-date=2016-07-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref> was the 83rd season of the [[Ekstraklasa]], [[Polish football league system|the top Polish professional league]] for [[association football]] clubs, since its establishment in [[1927 Ekstraklasa|1927]]. The league is operated by the Ekstraklasa SA.

The season started on 15 July 2016,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.90minut.pl/mecz.php?id_mecz=1229279 |title=Lotto Ekstraklasa 2016/2017 - Kolejka 1 |work=90minut.pl |access-date=15 July 2016}}</ref> running to 4 June 2017.<ref>{{cite web | title = Ramowy terminarz sezonu 2016/2017 |publisher = 90minut.pl |date = 16 March 2016 |url = http://www.90minut.pl/news/263/news2633738-Ramowy-terminarz-sezonu-2016-2017.html |access-date = 15 May 2016 }}</ref> After the 20th matchday the league was on winter break between 20 December 2016 and 9 February 2017. The regular season was played in a [[round-robin tournament]]. A total of 16 teams participated, 14 of which competed in the league during the 2015–16 season, while the remaining two were promoted from the [[2015–16 I liga|I liga]]. The fixtures were announced on 1 June 2016.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ekstraklasa.org/znamy-zestaw-par-na-sezon-201617/9|title=ZNAMY ZESTAW PAR NA SEZON 2016/17|website=www.ekstraklasa.org|date=1 June 2016|access-date=1 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160605145303/http://www.ekstraklasa.org/znamy-zestaw-par-na-sezon-201617/9|archive-date=5 June 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Each team played a total of 30 matches, half at home and half away. After 30th round (at the end of April 2017), league was split into two groups: ''championship round'' (top eight teams) and ''relegation round'' (bottom eight teams). Each team was play 7 more games (1-4 and 9-12 teams will play four times at home), starting with half the points achieved during the first phase of 30 matches. So, finally each team played a total of 37 matches. This is the fourth season to take place since the new playoff/playout rule has been introduced.

The defending champions were [[Legia Warsaw]], who won their 11th Polish title [[2015–16 Ekstraklasa|the previous season]].

==Teams==
Sixteen teams competed in the league – the top fourteen teams from the previous season, as well as two teams promoted from the [[2015–16 I liga|I liga]]. [[Arka Gdynia]] became the first team to be promoted.<ref>{{cite web | title = Czekali na to pięć lat, Arka Gdynia wraca do Ekstraklasy! | publisher = przegladsportowy.pl | date = 11 May 2016 | url = http://www.przegladsportowy.pl/pilka-nozna/i-liga,i-liga-arka-gdynia-awansowala-do-ekstraklasy,artykul,671756,1,359.html | access-date = 15 May 2016 | archive-date = 30 June 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160630135417/http://www.przegladsportowy.pl/pilka-nozna/i-liga,i-liga-arka-gdynia-awansowala-do-ekstraklasy,artykul,671756,1,359.html | url-status = dead }}</ref> They return to the league after a five-season absence. [[Wisła Płock]] returns to the top level nine years after their relegation.<ref>{{cite web | title = Wisła Płock awansowała do Ekstraklasy | publisher = 90minut | date = 20 May 2016 | url = http://www.90minut.pl/news/266/news2660991-Wisla-Plock-awansowala-do-Ekstraklasy.html | access-date = 20 May 2016 }}</ref> Termalica Bruk-Bet Nieciecza changed its name to Bruk-Bet Termalica Nieciecza.<ref>{{cite web | title = Terminarz Ekstraklasy 2016/2017 | publisher = 90minut | date = 1 June 2016 | url = http://www.90minut.pl/news/266/news2664920-Terminarz-Ekstraklasy-2016-2017.html | access-date = 6 June 2016 }}</ref>
